decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: Decline Curves and Future Royalty Cash Flow
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is c3b0e15b5f2d1cc1efe2cee13496b76870e05b287ccfd6e9ed7d2ea0fa646fb8; all 7 declared official sources passed live access review.
Production-data, curve-methodology, regional-metric, property-tax income-analysis, reserve-classification, and price-uncertainty claims remain bounded to their official government sources.

The article uses no fabricated owner records, well results, production volumes, decline rates, prices, reserves, dollar amounts, percentages, deductions, tax outcomes, testimonials, or owner-specific forecasts or value conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Production Decline Curve Analysis (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: EIA documents a specific production-decline routine that estimates hyperbolic parameters from observed well-level data, treats the first calendar month separately, normalizes later months, transitions to exponential decline at a defined threshold, and updates play assumptions as data change.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses this as a transparent public methodology example and does not claim that EIA validated any owner, well, curve parameters, reserve quantity, forecast horizon, or transaction value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas Production Data Query (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission Production Data Query provides general and specific query paths and states the processing date and loaded production-data period.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The source supports production-history retrieval and identity checks; the article does not treat Commission data as proof of title, decimal interest, payment terms, reserves, or owner cash flow.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas data sets available for download (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission describes lease-level, well-level, historical, statewide, master, disposition, and other production-related data sets, including their coverage and update cadence.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses these descriptions to preserve reporting-level and correction boundaries and does not equate a regulatory series with one owner’s statement allocation.

sources_inspected.label: U.S. Energy Information Administration Drilling Productivity Report FAQ (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: EIA explains that its regional legacy-production change separates new-well production from the changing production of an existing-well group and does not directly translate into a traditional individual-well decline curve.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article preserves the regional-versus-individual boundary and does not substitute regional averages for a particular lease, well, owner, reserve estimate, or transaction forecast.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Comptroller Manual for Discounting Oil and Gas Income (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Comptroller manual documents an income-discounting framework for Texas oil and gas property-tax appraisal, including amount, timing, discounting, and risk inputs.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article preserves the property-tax context and does not present the manual as a private-sale formula, reserve report, discount-rate prescription, or owner-specific valuation.

sources_inspected.label: SEC Division of Corporation Finance oil and gas rules interpretations (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: SEC staff interpretations preserve different certainty and evidence boundaries for proved, probable, and possible reserves and discuss documentation of reliable technology.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the guidance only to explain why reserve terminology and categories should not be attached casually to an owner worksheet; it does not classify any owner interest or supply a private forecast.

sources_inspected.label: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Energy Price Volatility and Forecast Uncertainty (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: EIA describes energy-price volatility, market-implied price bands, and the uncertainty surrounding base-case energy forecasts.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the source to support separate price scenarios and does not adopt a current price, promise a price path, or convert an EIA outlook into an owner-specific value.
